html:
If you are working out how to get PR in Sweden after study, begin with the part that many guides blur: a bachelor’s or master’s degree does not lead straight to permanent residence. The degree gets you to the next stage. Your permit history and employment record do the rest.

Most non-EU graduates finish their programme, use a job-seeking residence permit if needed, move to a qualifying work permit and apply for permanent residence after building enough eligible time.

Study permit → job-seeking residence permit → work permit → permanent residence permit

For a standard employee, that usually means holding a permit for work and working in Sweden for four of the previous seven years. Certain doctoral students, researchers and Swedish EU Blue Card holders can qualify through a three-year route.

This guide explains the July 2026 Sweden PR process, including salary figures, costs and qualifying periods.

Last checked against Swedish Migration Agency guidance on 14 July 2026.

Sweden PR Requirements for International Students

The main Sweden PR requirements for international students depend on the permit you hold after graduation. Time spent in Sweden matters, but the type of permit matters more.

Question

2026 position

Can a bachelor’s or master’s graduate receive PR immediately?

No

How long can the post-study permit last?

Up to one year

How much maintenance money is required?

SEK 10,656 per month

What is the adult post-study application fee?

SEK 1,500

What is the employee application fee?

SEK 2,200

What is the general work permit salary threshold?

SEK 34,470 per month

What is the lower threshold for an eligible former student’s first work permit?

SEK 28,725 per month

When can a standard employee apply for PR?

After four qualifying work years during the previous seven years

Is there a faster route for some doctoral or research applicants?

Yes, after three continuous years on eligible permits

What else is assessed?

Sustainable income, previous permit compliance and good conduct

EU and EEA citizens follow separate right-of-residence rules. The route below is for graduates who need Swedish permits.

What Changed in Sweden’s 2026 PR and Work Permit Rules?

Three updates deserve attention.

First, Sweden raised the general work permit salary threshold to 90% of the national median salary. The current figure is SEK 34,470 per month.

Second, former students who can apply for their first work permit from inside Sweden fall within an exempt group. Their salary must reach at least 75% of the median salary, currently SEK 28,725 per month. The role must still pay at least the level set by a collective agreement or normal practice in that occupation.

Third, from 13 July 2026, stricter good-conduct checks apply to residence permit applications. The Swedish Migration Agency may look beyond criminal convictions and consider repeated rule-breaking, unpaid debts, dishonest benefit claims or links to criminal or extremist networks.

They do not create direct PR after an ordinary degree. They make the study-to-work transition more important.

The Sweden PR Process After Study

1. Complete the Entire Programme

To use the graduate job-search route, you must complete a higher education programme lasting at least two semesters at a Swedish university or university college. You need to pass the whole programme, not simply attend the final term.

Use a degree certificate, transcript or verifiable Ladok record as proof, and apply before your study permit expires.

A surprisingly common delay starts with one missing result. The student has finished the dissertation, attended graduation and started applying for jobs, but one module still appears as incomplete in Ladok. On paper, the programme is not finished yet.

Students still choosing a country can compare long-term study options across Europe. The first graduate job often matters more than the headline PR period.

2. Apply for a Job-Seeking Residence Permit

After completing bachelor’s or master’s studies, you may apply for a residence permit to look for work or examine the possibility of starting a business. It can last for up to one year. After doctoral studies, the permit can last from one year to 18 months.

For a full 12-month permit in 2026, the basic maintenance calculation is:

SEK 10,656 × 12 = SEK 127,872

The application fee is SEK 1,500 for an adult and SEK 750 for a child. Extra monthly funds are required when an eligible partner or child applies with you.

Check the latest graduate job-search conditions before applying. The permit gives you time to find work. It does not count as qualifying employment.

3. Move from Study to a Work Permit

Once you find a suitable job, your employer starts the work permit process. You then complete your part of the application before your current permit expires.

You need a signed contract, appropriate pay and employer-funded health, life, occupational injury and occupational pension insurance. The terms must match a Swedish collective agreement or normal practice in the profession.

Eligible former students applying for their first work permit from inside Sweden are exempt from the general 90% salary rule. Their current floor is 75% of the median salary, or SEK 28,725 per month. The exemption normally applies for two years or, if the permit lasts longer, until it expires. A later extension may have to meet the general salary rule.

The rules for graduates moving into employment explain who can apply from within Sweden. Check them alongside the current work permit salary threshold.

Here is the catch: passing the numerical threshold does not guarantee that the job qualifies.

Imagine that Nadia finishes an MSc in data analytics and receives an offer of SEK 29,500 per month. The salary clears the former-student floor. Yet the application can still run into trouble if comparable roles normally pay more, the contract lacks enough detail or the employer has missed occupational pension insurance.

A well-known university may win Nadia an interview. It cannot repair a weak offer.

4. Build Four Clean Years of Qualifying Work

For the standard employee route, you must normally have held a work permit, met its conditions and worked in Sweden for four of the past seven years.

Ordinary bachelor’s and master’s study time does not usually count towards those four work years. The job-seeking period does not become qualifying employment time either.

Think about it this way. Nadia’s master’s degree ends in June 2026, and her qualifying work permit starts in February 2027. If she keeps valid permits and compliant employment without a damaging gap, she may reach four qualifying work years around February 2031.

The calculation is easy. Proving it can be harder.

Keep each contract, payslip, permit decision, Swedish Tax Agency record and insurance certificate. Recovering a four-year-old pension policy after an employer closes is rarely quick.

5. Apply for Permanent Residence with the Extension

Employees normally request a permanent residence permit when they apply to extend their work permit. You can apply once you have held and met the conditions of a permit for work and worked in Sweden for four of the previous seven years.

Only lawful, taxed income that exists when the case is decided counts. A promised promotion or possible future job does not.

For a single adult in 2026, you must have at least SEK 6,243 left each month after paying your share of housing costs. The amount covers ordinary living expenses such as food, clothing, hygiene, electricity, telephone and insurance.

A fixed-term contract can qualify if the income looks reliable and likely to continue. The employee application fee is currently SEK 2,200.

Review the employee extension and permanent residence rules before submitting. Work back through the entire permit period, not just the latest contract.

Does Study Time Count Towards PR in Sweden?

For most bachelor’s and master’s graduates using the employee route, no. Their ordinary study permit does not normally count towards the four qualifying work years.

Doctoral students and researchers have a different route. A person may qualify after three consecutive years with one or a combination of Swedish permits for doctoral studies, research, long-term research mobility or an EU Blue Card. The four-years-within-seven route can also remain relevant for eligible permit combinations.

The doctoral and research residence rules set out which periods can count. Swedish EU Blue Card holders should also check the rules for extending a Swedish Blue Card.

Physical presence and qualifying residence are not the same. The difference can shift a PR date by years.

Sweden PR Time by Route

Route

Time that normally counts

Common eligibility point

Bachelor’s or master’s graduate who becomes an employee

Qualifying work permit and employment time

Four years during the previous seven years

Doctoral student or researcher

Eligible doctoral, research or Swedish EU Blue Card periods

Three continuous years, or another qualifying combination

Swedish EU Blue Card holder

Swedish Blue Card and certain eligible combined periods

36 continuous months

EU or EEA graduate

Lawful right of residence

Permanent right of residence after five years

When people ask how many years to get PR in Sweden, they often mean only the qualifying period. Add the degree, job search and permit gaps to estimate your own timeline.

Documents to Keep for a Sweden Permanent Residence Application

Start collecting evidence when the first job begins.

Keep passport copies, permit decisions, degree evidence, contracts, job descriptions, payslips, PAYE tax records, employer certificates and proof of insurance. Add a certified translation when a document is not in Swedish or English.

Dates, occupation, salary and employer details should match throughout the file.

There is no prize for the thickest file. Ten relevant documents with matching facts are safer than forty pages that contradict one another.

Mistakes That Can Damage an Otherwise Strong PR Route

Counting every year in Sweden. Ordinary bachelor’s and master’s study time usually does not count towards the standard employee route.

Using an old salary figure. The previous SEK 13,000 figure is no longer the correct benchmark. The 2026 work permit rules use a percentage of the national median salary.

Checking salary but ignoring insurance. The authority can review employment conditions across the qualifying period, including health, life, occupational injury and pension insurance.

Changing employer or occupation without checking the permit. A change can require a fresh application. Check before the new job starts.

Applying after the current permit expires. A late application can remove your right to work while waiting, which can also undermine the financial maintenance test.

Ignoring debts or inaccurate benefit information. The stricter good-conduct assessment that began on 13 July 2026 can include repeated non-criminal misconduct as well as offences.

Fix problems while the records are recent. Four years later, even a simple correction can turn into a paper chase.

Are the Rules Different for Indian, Pakistani or Bangladeshi Graduates?

The core route is the same for most non-EU nationals. PR in Sweden for Indian students, Pakistani students or Bangladeshi students still depends on permit type, qualifying time, pay, insurance, income and conduct.

Document checks can differ, particularly for identity, civil status and accompanying family members.

EU and EEA citizens follow right-of-residence rules rather than the standard non-EU work permit route.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Sweden Give PR to International Students?

Not directly after an ordinary bachelor’s or master’s degree. PR in Sweden for international students normally becomes possible after the graduate moves to a qualifying work, doctoral, research or Swedish EU Blue Card route.

How to Get Permanent Residency in Sweden After Graduation?

Complete the programme, use the job-seeking permit if needed, secure qualifying work and move to the correct permit. Apply for permanent residence with the relevant extension once you meet the time, income and conduct conditions.

How Long Does It Take to Get PR in Sweden?

Most employees need four qualifying work years during the previous seven years. Certain doctoral students, researchers and Swedish EU Blue Card holders can qualify after three continuous years. The full Sweden PR time will usually be longer once study and job-search periods are included.

What Salary Does a Graduate Need for the First Work Permit?

An eligible former student applying from inside Sweden currently needs at least SEK 28,725 per month. The pay must also match the collective agreement or normal rate for the occupation. The general threshold is SEK 34,470 per month.

Can Part-Time Work Count Towards Permanent Residence?

It can help with the PR maintenance test if the jobs are lawful, taxed and reliable. The Swedish Migration Agency allows income from more than one part-time job to be combined for permanent residence when each job meets the relevant conditions.

This is different from the first graduate work permit, where two or more jobs cannot be combined to meet the employment requirements.

Is a Permanent Contract Required?

No. A fixed-term contract may qualify if the income is sustainable and likely to continue. A contract ending soon after the decision date will naturally receive closer scrutiny.

Is There a Swedish Language Requirement for PR?

The standard employee route does not currently list a general Swedish-language test among its core permanent residence requirements. Language ability still helps with employment and daily life, but citizenship follows separate rules.

How Long Does the PR Decision Take?

There is no single processing time. Check the Swedish Migration Agency’s latest figures for your permit type; incomplete files usually take longer.

Final Checklist

Before applying, check that you completed the programme, filed every permit on time, built enough qualifying residence, met the salary and insurance rules, kept complete records and can still support yourself after housing costs. Your conduct must also meet the rules in force when the case is decided.

That is how to get PR in Sweden after study without relying on an outdated salary figure or assuming that every year in the country counts.

Students comparing long-term options can also look at Finland’s route after graduation and Germany’s post-study settlement route. When the course, budget and permit plan need to fit together, book a planning call with an adviser.
